events.what: Bradford claims a full proof for all primes via a covering-system argument over Type I/II solutions
events.credibility_reason: Specific identified error in the key step, recorded in the record's disputes: 'taking the first primes modulo different moduli doesn't create a covering system', and the six hard residue classes mod 840 are not excluded. No answer from the author is recorded.

events.what: Cluster of preprints (Dyachenko, Farah, Ghermoul, Mballa, Xu, Bello-Hernández et al.) giving explicit families covering sub-classes of p ≡ 1 mod 4 or of the hard classes mod 840
events.credibility_reason: The record says it is unclear whether any of them go beyond pre-2024 coverage (Mordell, Elsholtz and others). Farah's 804/840 classes is fewer than the classical Mordell coverage of all but 6 of 840. Density-one explicit solutions were already known. Adding more covered congruence sub-classes does not settle any restriction of the bullet the literature did not already have. The preprints are mutually unreconciled and uncited.

events.what: Pseudonymous 'The Clankers' Zenodo postings with invented terminology
events.credibility_reason: Pseudonymous, invented terminology, cites Reddit posts, no uptake on a landmark problem.

judgement.doubts: The Bradford claim fields (event, credited_humans) are left as the record's most salient event, but they set nothing. If an expert later confirms that one of the residue-class preprints covers a restriction that was genuinely new, it would be a case (partial). Nothing in the record shows that.

corrections.why: F6/F4: The status rested on Bradford's claim, which the record's disputes show was knocked down by a specific error: the covering system does not cover, and the six hard classes mod 840 are left out. A knocked-down claim is not progress. Verification to 10^18 is instances. The residue-class preprints move no bound, and the record itself doubts they go beyond pre-2024 coverage (Farah's 804/840 is below Mordell's classical 834/840). Nothing survives, so the status is open, as the record's competing_reading argued.
F6: No credible event after the snapshot settles or bounds anything on this bullet. See the status correction.
